description.narrative: IFC is considering two senior loans to support the development, construction, and operation of two offshore windfarms (Baltyk II and Baltyk III) that are being developed through a Joint Venture between Equinor Wind Power and Polenergia S.A. (the Projects). Each of the two offshore wind power projects will comprise 50 wind turbines (i.e., 100 in total), an offshore substation and inter-array cabling, and will have an installed capacity of 720MW (1.44GW in total). The Projects were awarded a 25-year Contract for Difference (CfD) tariff that was set by the Government of Poland.

The project will add clean energy capacity that contributes to lowering the carbon footprint of the electricity system in Poland, a country dominated by coal-powered electricity generation and where electricity represents 49 percent of its total energy-related GHG emissions. Moreover, it would facilitate the decommissioning of the lignite-fired plants in Poland, corresponding to GHG emission reductions of nearly 3.9 mn tCO2 per year. It is also expected to increase renewable power in Poland by adding offshore wind power at a competitive LCOE, corresponding to almost 25 percent of the Polish Governments installed offshore wind capacity target of 5.9 GW by 2030. The project is contributing to market creation by contributing to enhanced resilience by demonstrating large-scale employment of alternative energy technologies that contribute to diversifying the electricity generation mix in Poland, which is currently heavily reliant on coal, and where wind power only represents 10.9 percent of the total installed electricity capacity.
